title: One Machinery, Many Projects
eyebrow: The plan for the machinery every project shares. Waiting on your go.

options.label: Go
options.say: Build it in this shape, in this order.

options.label: Adjust
options.say: The shape is close but I want something changed — I will say what in chat.

options.label: Not now
options.say: Leave the machinery where it is; the beads board keeps borrowing.

questions.note: Going costs roughly two sittings before anything visible changes, and the visible part — the beads project running like the racing one — lands right after. Not going leaves every new project to borrow tools by hand.

content.label: What you get
content.lead: Any project of yours runs the way the racing one runs — same ticket quality, same gates, same run of steps, same pages — without borrowing anything.

items: An agent filing a beads fault tomorrow lands it on the beads board with nobody watching — the routing is the machinery's, not a habit.
A commit in any project names that project's own cards and is accepted by that project's own gate.
An improvement to the machinery lands once and every project has it the same day.
A new project joins by writing one short declaration, not by copying tools.

blocks.label: Three things this absorbs
blocks.text: The card about the beads checkout borrowing the pour tools with an overridden address, and the card about the commit gate only recognising its home board's ids, are both closed into this job. The third part of your move instruction — future agents filing beads work on the beads board without being told — is carried here too, so the move job keeps only the split and the move.

content.label: The line: what is shared, what stays a project's own
content.lead: Shared is everything that makes work honest and argues the same way everywhere. A project keeps exactly the five things that differ by subject.

rows: The ticket standard: what a card must say before it exists
Its board and its card prefix
The gates: what refuses a bad close, a silent question, a commit with no card
Its vocabulary of subjects, in its own words
The run of steps a job walks, and the review by someone who did not write it
How a change proves itself — the racing game renders and measures; the beads app drives its screen and photographs it
The plain-words rules and the report pages
Its specialist helpers and its machine guards

blocks.label: Why the line sits there
blocks.text: Each item on the right is exactly what the inventory found hard-wired into the tools today — the racing project's list of subjects, the place its finished work lands, its own name inside the reviewer's introduction, its build traps. Those are the very lines that stop the machinery travelling; pulled into a declaration, everything else moves unchanged.

content.label: How it stays one machinery
content.lead: One live home, run in place; a copy inside a project is refused by a check, the same way report tools already are.

items: The machinery's own test run comes back green from the shared home against every project's declaration — a project with a stale declaration is refused by name, not silently mis-served.
Nothing is versioned per project, so there is no drift to reconcile.
The reporting tools already live this way and stay exactly where they are; this job does not touch them.

content.label: What keeps standing while it moves
content.lead: Both running builds finish their current piece untouched; the switch happens between pieces, never under one.

rows: The chat build in the beads project, mid-piece
The machinery lands between its pieces; its files and its cards are not touched.
Every racing-project session, using today's paths
The old paths keep answering through thin forwarders until each session restarts; behaviour is identical either side of the switch.
The move of the 61 beads cards
Queued behind this job on purpose — it runs under the new machinery, so the boards it writes already understand both checkouts.

decisions.title: The machinery moves to a home of its own and every project runs it in place — never a copy
decisions.why: One live copy is what makes an improvement land everywhere the same day. The report tools already prove the pattern; a copies check makes forking it impossible rather than impolite.

decisions.title: The shared-versus-own line is drawn at the five declared things
decisions.why: Board and prefix, subject vocabulary, proof of change, where finished work lands, specialist helpers. Each is exactly what was found hard-wired today, and each would make the shared core lie if it stayed hard-wired.

decisions.title: Every gate reads the board of the checkout the work lands in, never the session's home
decisions.why: This is the fix that closes the borrowed-address card and the commit-gate card, and it is what routes tomorrow's beads fault to the beads board with nobody watching.

decisions.title: The racing project is unchanged through the switch
decisions.why: Thin forwarders keep every old path answering until sessions restart; its whole test run must come back green from the shared home before anything is removed.

decisions.title: The card move waits for this job
decisions.why: Moving 61 cards onto a board whose gates cannot yet read them would recreate today's problem on the other side. The move job is queued behind this one on the beads board, split already written on its card.

decisions.title: Domain guards and specialist helpers stay home
decisions.why: The render checks, the machine's build traps and the car, track and tree researchers are the racing project's subject knowledge, not machinery. The beads project grows its own equivalents — the screen-driving proof is already wired there.

next.if_nothing: Nothing moves: the beads board keeps borrowing tools with an overridden address, and the 61-card move stays queued.

steps.step: The machinery stands in its own home and the racing project comes through its whole test run green from it, unchanged
The beads checkout pours its own cards and its commits are accepted by its own gate — no borrowed address anywhere
The racing checkout runs from the shared home; nothing visibly different
The shared skills follow, and each project's declaration is written
The 61 beads cards move and both boards read clean
